etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From New Latin ephemerus, from Ancient Greek ἐφήμερος (ephḗmeros), the more common form of ἐφημέριος (ephēmérios, “of, for, or during the day, living or lasting but for a day, short-lived, temporary”), from ἐπί (epí, “on”) + ἡμέρα (hēméra, “day”).
senses: Lasting for a short period of time.
(biology) Existing for only one day, as with some flowers, insects, and diseases.
Something which lasts for a short period of time.
